notes: 1.11: fixed things you moved with Built-ins landing on their neighbours (a bed in the forge, the forge's name following the bed) after 1.10 took the tent away: the tent's place is kept, moves now remember what they moved and find it again, and Put everything back clears an island's moves; a swapped camp building stands right behind its keeper; typing an island's text, ticket or menu look no longer rebuilds the island (its name and camp name rebuild once when you leave the box); Plinko's board shows (its frame was in front of it); things moved with Built-ins turn all the way round (they stopped at 90°); a big bed of your own is solid and you can sleep from anywhere round its edge. 1.10: the enchanting table stands on the ground on every Studio island (it used the last island's ground), and ✥ Built-ins can move, turn, size or hide it; floating names on anything: placed things get size and height, and anything the game built (the forge, BED, the Ferryman, the casino, the enchanting table) can have its names changed, hidden or added; names no longer vanish when an island rebuilds; with ✥ Built-ins on you can still click what you placed (a portal); the usual tent is an A-frame now, and a bed of your own stands alone. 1.9: a Bed slot in the Islands tab's ARCHITECTURE: your model replaces the bed you sleep in (a small model picked as the bed hut counts too), and ✦ Restyle with Claude gives the casino a new look any time, from the island or what you describe. 1.8: the casino moves by itself to your newest island and is re-skinned for it, outside and in: its name and sign line, colours, a spire, dome, crown or flat roof, which side it stands on, and the hall's wallpaper, carpet, trim and chandeliers. Ask Claude designs one for every island; without one it takes the island's own colours. Fixed: the shop menu no longer clashes with the casino's. 1.7: Ask Claude can invent a whole island: its own architecture (the bed hut, forge, trading post and witch's hut rebuilt in one style), shops with their own keepers, buildings and things to buy, models, landmarks, trees, animals and people, three requests at a time; each island gets its own menu look (colours, a heading font, corners), always readable. Shops work by hand too (🛒 Shop in the Place tab, or the Islands tab), and you can swap any camp building for one of your props. 1.6: ⟳ Sync brings in what's on GitHub (releases and Studio updates) and keeps your own work: islands, trees, props, animals, people and placed things from both sides are kept, and islands already on GitHub keep their rebirths while yours move after them, trees and all; npm run studio:update does the same from a terminal, then installs and starts the Studio. You can walk onto the docks again: the Iceberg's arrivals and Rebirth 6 docks, and every Studio island's. 1.5: the People Maker (new kinds of people: hair, hats, beards, faces, clothes, what they hold and say, or ask Claude; islands get residents too), the top bar wraps instead of pushing Release and Play off screen, and "Gives off real light" switches off properly instead of piling up. 1.4: your work is also kept in Documents/Tree Sim 4 Studio (with dated backups), and after an update or a fresh download the Studio offers to bring it back; Ask Claude can do anything with an island: new outlines (long, lobed), walkable islands joined by bridges, new buildings it builds from parts, and the game's props put around it; you can make all of that by hand too. 1.3: move, turn, resize or hide anything the game built (beds, stalls, signs, rocks), with its collisions, label and press-F spot; sculpt your islands' ground with Raise, Lower, Flatten and Erase brushes. 1.2: your trees grow (the Studio shows every tree an island can grow; an island can let every tree grow from the start), Unused and On islands tree lists, trees in the Islands tab with how common each one is, the ecosystem (animals, ground cover, fireflies), the Animal Maker (parts with legs, wings and tails that move, or ask Claude), each island's own materials and axes, and Ask Claude invents all of it with the island. 1.1: the Prop Maker, island features, Ask Claude for islands, your own themes
